title: Replace the trust workflow with an identically-named no-op that reports success

prerequisites: A malicious PR author who edits .github/workflows/safeinstall-trust.yml in the PR
attacker.goal: Satisfy the required status check by name while the workflow does nothing, so a required-check-by-name ruleset passes a tampered PR.

startingState: The PR rewrites the trust workflow to a no-op that keeps the workflow and job names, aiming to pass the required 'trust-base' check without verifying anything.
vulnerableVersion: n/a — defended on two axes: pull_request_target loads the workflow definition from the protected base branch (a PR cannot change what runs for its own check), and editing the workflow file is enforcement-zone drift the trust check flags
expectedVerdict: fail: the neutered workflow fails verification on content (the base-loaded definition runs, not the PR's), and the edit is trust-surface drift
regressionTest: safeinstall-verifier: test/run-adversarial.sh case neutered-same-name; local: tests/workflow-security.test.ts
provenance: RFC-001 §13 K1; closed by the external verifier repo + base-loaded workflow
